newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault creates new management units.
newsitem.headline: Renault creates new management units.

text.p: Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer has created two management units -- a Mercosur unit for the South American business and a light commercial vehicles unit to carry out group strategies, the company said on Monday.

It has also changed some of the reporting lines, giving executive vice president Carlos Ghosn -- recently hired away from Michelin -- responsibility for the Mercosur unit and for the project management departments for passenger cars which had previously reported to Georges Douin.

Luc-Alexandre Menard, currently senior vice president, market area France, will head the Mercosur unit and be appointed chairman of COFAL, the holding company which controls Renault's operations in Argentina and Brazil. Menard will report to Ghosn.
"Renault is counting on this centre of operations (the Mercosur unit) to boost its sales outside Europe by the year 2000," the company said in a statement.
The international operations department, headed by Manuel Gomez, will report to Douin, a senior vice president.
Francis Stahl, currently senior vice president, corporate controller, will head the light commercial vehicles unit and report to Patrick Faure, head of marketing and sales.
